ai.description: Bibron's Skink reaches 6–8 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with a distinct dark lateral band and a pale vertebral stripe. Key features include a pointed snout and smooth, overlapping scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis bibronii* is best distinguished by the presence of a single pair of enlarged nuchal scales behind the parietals, a feature absent in most other Indian *Eutropis*.
ai.habitat: Bibron's skink inhabits coastal sandy areas and scrub forests in southern India and Sri Lanka, often found among leaf litter or under vegetation near the shoreline.
ai.behavior: Bibron's skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: Bibron's skink is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: Bibron's Skink is endemic to the southern Indian peninsula, primarily inhabiting the coastal plains and dry forests of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Andhra Pradesh.
